transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is in southern China, where he's scheduled to hold his first trilateral
meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports Trump says he wants to discuss nuclear arms control and
help with Iran.
"It'll be the first time the three leaders who manage the world's biggest nuclear arsenals
sit down together.
There are questions about what substance will come out of the meetings, especially when
China has shown little interest in reducing its nuclear weapons.
But this gathering, like many gatherings of foreign leaders, is also about the photo op.
It's a chance to demonstrate Trump's influence abroad after the devastating midterm elections.
Trump wants to be seen as a president who can pick up the phone and get America's biggest
adversaries around a table to get things done.
The test is whether Trump's personalized form of diplomacy will work, especially when he's
been politically weakened back home."
Franco, Ordonez, NPR News.
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic said today it has put nearly 1 billion shares
on the market at a price of $83 per share in a record-breaking initial public offering,
and Piers John Ruich has the story.
Just five years old, Anthropic is a powerhouse of the AI world with a clawed family of models.
Its IPO had been widely anticipated, and brings in over $81.3 billion.
That exceeds the $75 billion that Elon Musk's SpaceX raised in its IPO earlier this year.
Anthropic's listing had strong demand despite coming at a time of growing concern about
a possible AI bubble.
Its shares will start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol A-N-T,
and Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Congressman Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated for House Speaker when the Democrats take
control of Congress in January, and Piers Claudio Grisales reports.
House Democrats voted during a closed-door meeting, 251 to 11, in support of Hakeem Jeffries'
nomination.
Afterwards, the current House Minority Leader told reporters his caucus will work to deliver
for the American people.
Our job is to fight mega-extremism, not each other, to fight mega-extremism, and to get
big things done.
Several incoming, more left-wing House members who did not support Jeffries' bid said they're
still pushing for a more aggressive agenda to address affordability, immigration and
other issues.
The House floor will hold its vote for Speaker on the first day of the new Congress next
year, on January 3.
Claudio Grisales, NPR News, the Capitol.
Outgoing Louisiana Republican Senator Bill Cassidy, who chairs the Senate Health Committee,
said they would not consider the White House's pick to lead the National Science Foundation,
Jim O'Neill.
Cassidy said O'Neill did not do enough to stand up for science during his time as Acting
Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
O'Neill does not have an advanced science degree or research experience.
This is NPR News.
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian American citizenship has been convicted of U.S. charges
related to the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovanel Moise.
Christian Emmanuel Sannong was found guilty on all charges, including conspiring to kill
Moise.
Haiti hasn't had a president since the killing and is planning a presidential election next
year.
Researchers are developing brain implants that can help restore people's speech and
movement.
As NPR's Ping Huang reports, these technologies can even help them sing.
A 58-year-old trained singer had lost much of her ability to speak and sing due to ALS,
a disease that destroys nerve cells that control muscle movement.
Maitreyi Wairakar is a neuroscientist at UC Davis.
She and her colleagues designed an implant that connects to parts of the singer's brain
related to speech, pitch, and tone.
We designed a task to enable her to sing a musical scale.
We asked her to sing a typical major scale, and we were able to decode all the notes that
she sang with very high accuracy.
The implant records her brain signals into a computer, which translates them into commands.
The technology is still largely experimental and was presented at the Society for Neuroscience
conference.
Ping Huang, NPR News.
Officials at Grand Canyon National Park are easing water restrictions, meaning hotels
on the south rim will once again be able to accommodate overnight guests after major flooding
in August affected water service.
Park officials urge visitors to conserve by taking shorter showers and turning off faucets
when not in use.
